subject: Premium assurance pilot — uptime ladder & concession proposal
body:
From: Luke Hart <luke.hart@acadia.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-27T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Premium assurance — uptime bands for a short pilot

Hi Ben,

We’re evaluating Redwood for a three-month pilot and need a clear picture on your premium support tiers. Two quick asks: 1) What uptime bands do you offer (and any associated credits) for pilot vs. committed contracts? 2) Can you outline response windows and escalation coverage for a prioritized lane during the pilot?

Also, Acadia’s procurement asked whether a short-term pilot could get a one-time concession on price (we’d like to run 3 months at a reduced rate to validate the failover/latency characteristics). Please include any onboarding/consulting credit you’d bundle.

Timing: procurement would like an estimate by COB PT tomorrow so we can move the pilot into our vendor approval queue.

Thanks,

Luke Hart
Head of Platform
Acadia Analytics
Phone: +1 415-555-0123

Hi Luke — great to hear from you and excited you’re running a pilot. I’ve attached a short SKU table that maps our uptime bands and standard crediting approach. High level: 99.9% / 99.95% / 99.99% map to standard, enhanced, and premium bands — each has a defined credit slab in the event of a breach. For a 3-month pilot we can do a one-time concession: a pilot discount and 8 hours of onboarding credits.

Two quick clarifications that will help me firm up numbers for procurement:
- Expected monthly spend during the pilot (ballpark)
- Whether you need a named escalation contact (we can include 24/7 on-call for premium lane but it’s an add-on)

I’ll loop in pricing/finance internally and get back with a firm concession matrix by EOD PT tomorrow. Draft SOW attached for your review — this will let us scope onboarding hours.

Best,

Olga — any constraints from finance on revenue recognition or minimums for SOW-based pilots? Karthik/Marissa — would 15% + onboarding materially impact margins or set a bad precedent on tiering?

Ben — thanks for the heads up. I recommend the following, balancing revenue and a competitive pilot:

1) Pilot concession: 15% off list for the 3-month pilot (applied as one-time credit on first invoice).
2) Onboarding: include 8 hours free onboarding + 4 hours of complimentary healthcheck during month 2.
3) Uptime bands for pilot:
   - Pilot base (99.90%): standard breach credit 10% of that month’s invoice
   - Pilot enhanced (99.95%): 15% credit
   - Pilot premium (99.99%): 25% credit
   (Note: credits are capped at the monthly invoice amount)
4) Escalation: recommended we offer named on-call for the premium lane as an optional paid retainer. For the pilot we can provide business-hours named escalation contact only (no 24/7).

Olga — if finance needs protective language, we should require the SOW to include a conversion clause: if Acadia converts to a committed plan within 60 days of pilot end, the pilot discount is applied to the first full paid month(s) of the committed term. If they do not convert, the pilot concession is non-recoupable. That preserves revenue while giving the customer an incentive to convert.

If everyone is good, I’ll sign off and Ben can send formal offer.

Hi Luke — thanks for the patience while we coordinated internally. Quick summary of the approved pilot offer:

- Pilot length: 3 months
- Pilot concession: 15% off list applied as a one-time credit on month 1 invoice
- Onboarding: 8 hours included + one 4-hour healthcheck in month 2
- Uptime bands & credits (pilot):
  • 99.90% — standard (10% credit cap per month)
  • 99.95% — enhanced (15% credit cap per month)
  • 99.99% — premium (25% credit cap per month)
- Escalation coverage: business-hours named escalation contact included for pilot. 24/7 on-call is available as a paid retainer — estimate provided in attached SKU table.
- Conversion protection: the SOW includes a 60-day conversion clause — if Acadia converts to a committed plan within 60 days of pilot end, the pilot concession will be applied to the first paid month(s) of the committed term per the terms in the SOW. If not, concession is not recouped.

Next steps: please review the attached Draft_SOW_Acadia.pdf and the SKU table. If that looks good I can issue a pilot SOW for signature and we’ll schedule a kickoff the week after countersignature. If you need a slightly higher concession to pull procurement through, let me know and I’ll escalate (we have some flexibility if we get a signed SOW).

Looping in Marissa for commercial alignment on timeline — Marissa, we’ll need onboarding scheduling and an onboarding owner once they sign.

Best regards,
